title: ScreenConnect RMM+ extension default/blank API secret (CVE-2026-127063) abused to push rogue clients and SCKit to managed endpoints
why: ConnectWise (as CNA) assigned CVE-2026-127063 on Nov 12 to the RMM+ extension's default static API secret. Huntress links the Nov 11 SCKit incident (288 endpoints, 48 orgs, commands with no matching logins) to RMM+ 1.0.31/1.0.32 accepting a blank key. ConnectWise disabled RMM+ in about 400 partner environments. No fixed RMM+ version exists. CVE-2026-127063 is not in CISA KEV (the earlier KEV entry CVE-2026-84869 covers only the client spread step), and there is no Microsoft guidance. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: On on-prem ScreenConnect, disable and uninstall RMM+ and related extensions now. Review Run Command and Toolbox history since Nov 11 for mass commands or ScreenConnect installer downloads. Make sure technician clients are on 26.6.5 or later.
product: DataComm RMM+ third-party extension for ConnectWise ScreenConnect (Huntress: 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 accept a blank key); no fixed version announced

title: PaperCut NG/MF auth-bypass + class-loading RCE chain (CVE-2026-81578/82078): Hunt.io exposes AI-driven attacker toolkit and a second XML-RPC RCE path
why: Not ahead: CISA added both CVEs to KEV on Aug 31, 2026. New this run: an OTX pulse of Hunt.io research describing the operator's exposed AI toolkit and a second RCE route through the XML-RPC API, which needs weak API token and network controls rather than a new CVE.
action: Confirm PaperCut is on Emergency Patch Release 3 or a current maintenance release, set an explicit XML-RPC API token and lock the API allowlist down. If the server was internet-facing between Aug 15 and Sep 11, hunt for user-lookup.* config changes, unexpected files under custom/web/ and chisel or cron persistence.
product: PaperCut NG and PaperCut MF (all versions before Emergency Patch Release 3; current maintenance releases 26.0.5, 25.0.13, 24.1.10)

title: Xen Orchestra VSA-2026-062: vendor-confirmed exploited auth bypass to admin and XCP-ng root takeover (no CVE yet)
why: Vates' advisory VSA-2026-062 (Nov 10) says the flaw is actively exploited by a named threat actor; BleepingComputer, THN and SC Media report it. No CVE assigned, so nothing in CISA KEV. Ostorlab and Rescana confirmed on Nov 11: still no CVE and not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Update to Xen Orchestra 6.9.2 / 6.10.1 (xo-server 5.211.2 / 5.213.1), take XO off the internet, check for the pivot2 VM and hvm_serial:file configs listed in VSA-2026-062, and rotate all secrets.
product: Xen Orchestra / XOA before 6.9.2 (stable) / 6.10.1 (latest); xo-server before 5.211.2 / 5.213.1

title: Turla 'Cereal' toolset hides in Microsoft Exchange transport pipeline to steal government NATO/EU email
why: ESET published (Nov 10) a new Turla toolset found on government Exchange servers in Kazakhstan and Romania that injects into EdgeTransport.exe and uses the Exchange server itself as C2; IOCs are on ESET's GitHub. There is no CVE, KEV entry or Microsoft guidance on Cereal in the sources seen, and the initial-access vector is unknown. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Hunt on on-prem Exchange servers for foreign modules loaded in EdgeTransport.exe, unexpected files in the .NET native image cache and encrypted requests to /owa/sdds/ or /autodiscover/proxyservice/, using ESET's published IOCs.
product: Microsoft Exchange Server (on-premises; affected builds not disclosed)

title: wfx-loot: 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts push a CI secret stealer; secrets taken from 1,800+ repos, with AWS and Entra ID persistence
why: Aikido, OX Security, SafeDep and StepSecurity report a live campaign since Nov 10: stolen tokens for 4,837 GitHub accounts opened ~62-66k probe PRs and the stealer ran in at least 1,806 repositories, still ongoing on Nov 12 with exfil moved to Telegram. The payload adds wfx-ci-* federated credentials to Entra ID apps and rewrites AWS role trust policies, which survive secret rotation. There is no CVE (no product bug), so no CISA KEV entry, and no Microsoft or GitHub guidance appeared in the sources reviewed. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Search your GitHub org for PRs titled "docs: dependency audit notes" or wfx-docs branches since Nov 10; for any hit revoke that account's tokens and rotate every secret its workflows could reach, then hunt Entra ID for federated credentials named wfx-ci-* and AWS sessions named wfx-*.
vendor: GitHub (abuse of stolen developer tokens; no product flaw)
product: GitHub Actions workflows and npm postinstall hooks in any repository a compromised account can write to (since Nov 10, 2026)

title: MongoDB Server pre-auth use-after-free in replication catch-up (9.5); public PoC on GitHub
why: A GitHub PoC (indexed by Sploitus Nov 11) reproduces the unauthenticated use-after-free as a crash/memory corruption against 8.0.34; MongoDB says it knows of no exploitation. Not in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Upgrade replica-set MongoDB servers to the fixed release for your branch and make sure mongod ports are not reachable from untrusted networks.
product: MongoDB Server replica-set members (incl. shard/config servers) before 9.0.7 / 8.3.16 / 8.0.37 / 7.0.48 / 6.0.30 / 5.0.35 / 4.4.32; standalone mongod not affected

title: PostgreSQL CVE-2026-6460 type confusion: low-privileged database user to OS code execution, RCE technique now public
why: Researcher Mehmet Ince published a write-up turning the 22-year-old type confusion into code execution, and an independent researcher reproduced the crash with four SQL statements as a zero-privilege role (dev.to); the item hit Hacker News today. OffSeq and SecurityOnline report no exploitation, and it is not in CISA KEV. Hosted PostgreSQL services may be exposed, but no cloud-provider statement was found. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Upgrade to PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 or 14.25 (14 is now end-of-life), prioritising multi-tenant servers, and until then remove CREATE privileges from untrusted roles.
product: PostgreSQL before 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 and 14.25 (part of a 52-CVE release on Nov 12, 2026)

title: SGLang inference-engine RCE exploited to breach NEAR AI (no CVE, versions or upstream fix named)
why: NEAR AI's Nov 9 incident report says an attacker exploited an SGLang RCE on Nov 8 to run code on an inference server and pivot internally; it reported the bug to SGLang. No CVE, affected versions or upstream fix have been named, and nothing is in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Keep SGLang servers off the internet behind authenticated proxies, watch the SGLang repository for a security release, and rotate any secrets reachable from inference hosts.
product: SGLang (open-source LLM inference engine); affected versions not disclosed

title: Apify breach (Nov 9-10): attacker accessed internal systems; customer billing data and 2FA recovery codes exposed, all API tokens rotated
why: Apify's status page confirms an unauthorized third party accessed internal systems on Nov 9-10, detected Nov 11. Customer notices report exposed emails, billing details and 2FA recovery codes, and some GitHub OAuth connections were revoked. There is no CVE, so nothing is in KEV, and no Microsoft coverage was seen. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Replace Apify API tokens in every pipeline, set up 2FA again, review GitHub activity for any account linked to Apify, and warn finance about invoice phishing that uses real billing details.
product: Apify platform (hosted)

title: Cursor confirms breach let attackers publish a malicious Claude Code extension in its marketplace, after credentials were stolen from Fireworks AI
why: Not ahead: Microsoft Security already published on the trojanized Claude Code extension on Oct 30 (earlier runs). New on Nov 14: Cursor confirmed the breach that enabled it, tracing it to credentials stolen from Fireworks AI.
action: Inventory Cursor/VS Code-family installs for the trojanized Claude Code extension build flagged in October and rotate any credentials and tokens available on those developer machines.
product: Cursor IDE extension marketplace (trojanized Claude Code extension)

title: Fortinet FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer pre-auth RCE: FGFM (126261), JSON-RPC API (126170), OFTP SQLi (126262)
why: Fortinet published FG-IR-26-275/219/276 on Nov 10. FGFM and OFTP flaws are unauthenticated, and the JSON-RPC injection (126170, CVSS 9.8) gives unauthenticated code execution when the API is enabled. Fortinet says none are known exploited and none are in CISA KEV. A Sploitus 'PoC' listing is unverified. Earlier FGFM bugs (FortiJump) were mass-exploited. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Upgrade FortiManager to 8.0.1/7.6.8/7.4.6/7.2.9 (and FAZ per FG-IR-26-276), set 'rpc-permit none' on admin profiles if JSON API is not needed, and restrict FGFM/OFTP to known FortiGate addresses.
product: FortiManager 8.0.0, 7.6.0-7.6.7, 7.4.0-7.4.5, 7.2.0-7.2.8 (FGFM); FortiManager/FortiAnalyzer with JSON API enabled (126170) or FAZ features/OFTP (126262)

title: Apache HTTP Server mod_http2 unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-119618): Red Hat cites a reliable exploit in public research, Wiz says no exploit yet
why: Red Hat's CVE page says 'public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit' against a default mod_http2 server but does not name it. Wiz says no exploit is available and no attacks are reported. A Sploitus-indexed lab repo only shows sanitizer-level reproduction. Not in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Upgrade to httpd 2.4.71 or the distro-patched mod_http2. Until then, remove h2/h2c from the Protocols directive on internet-facing servers.
product: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 with HTTP/2 enabled; standalone mod_h2 2.0.8 through 2.0.42

title: Fortinet FortiOS November batch: unauthenticated super-admin command execution via HA packets (126259) plus OSPF/BGP routing flaws
why: Fortinet published FG-IR-26-273 on Nov 10 (CVSS 9.8 per NVD). Its HA virtual patch is labelled '0day', and its own scores mark some bugs as having exploit code. Fortinet reports no attacks, there is no public PoC, and none of the batch is in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Upgrade FortiOS to 8.0.1, or to 7.6.8/7.4.13/7.2.14 when they ship. Until then, apply the FortiGuard HA virtual patch and keep HA/FGSP sync traffic on a dedicated non-routed segment.
product: FortiOS 8.0.0, 7.6.0-7.6.7, 7.4.0-7.4.12, 7.2.0-7.2.13 (HA FGSP with standalone-config-sync, or autoscale)

title: Fortinet FortiMail unauthenticated RCE: path traversal (126147), HA join-request command injection (126148), SMTP format string (126163)
why: Fortinet advisories FG-IR-26-199/200 (Nov 10, CVSS 9.8) list these as unauthenticated code execution and 'Known Exploited: No'. Rescana confirmed they were not in CISA KEV on Nov 11. A GitHub 'PoC' for 126147 indexed on Sploitus is only a simulated lab, not a working exploit against FortiMail. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Upgrade FortiMail to 8.0.2/7.6.7/7.4.9 (migrate off 7.2), and restrict the management interface and HA ports to trusted networks.

title: Synology DSM pre-auth SQL injection in Auth API (9.8) and rsync auth bypass allow unauthenticated arbitrary file read/write
why: Synology SA-26:19 (Nov 10, CVE published Nov 12) fixes an unauthenticated SQL injection with arbitrary file write. Viettel, who reported it, calls it a pre-auth zero-click RCE. No exploitation or public PoC yet and not in CISA KEV, while Synology NAS devices are already being hit by ransomware via an older DSM flaw. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Update DSM to 7.2.1-69057-13 / 7.2.2-72806-10 / 7.3.2-86009-5 / 7.4.1-90080-1 or later, and keep DSM (ports 5000/5001) and rsync off the internet.

title: iOS 'worse_query' sandbox escape PoC lets a malicious app read other apps' files; no Apple fix confirmed
why: Researcher forcequitOS published a developer PoC on GitHub Nov 8 and Binance warned users Nov 10; Apple's iOS 27.2.1/26.7.3 notes (Nov 9) do not mention it and no fix is confirmed. No exploitation or thefts reported; no CVE, not in KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Update managed iPhones/iPads to iOS 27.2.1 or 26.7.3, block sideloaded/enterprise-signed apps via MDM, and tell users not to keep secrets in plaintext on the device.
product: Apple iOS 26.0-26.7.2 and 27.2 per researcher (Binance lists 26.7.1, 27.0.1, 27.2); unclear whether iOS 27.2.1 / 26.7.3 fix it

title: Ivanti Endpoint Manager unauthenticated SQL injection to RCE (9.8) and Cloud Services Application missing auth (9.4)
why: Ivanti's November EPM advisory and NVD (Nov 10) describe a remote unauthenticated SQL injection in the EPM Core leading to code execution; no exploitation or public PoC reported, not in CISA KEV. Ivanti EPM bugs have been targeted after past disclosures. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Upgrade EPM Core to 2024 SU8, update the Cloud Services Application past 5.0.8, and keep the EPM Core and CSA consoles off the internet.
product: Ivanti Endpoint Manager before 2024 SU8; Ivanti Cloud Services Application 5.0.8

title: React Server Components unauthenticated RCE in rare typed-array cases (react-server-dom-*)
why: React published GHSA-xqc2-xf4c-x3h3 / CVE-2026-126187 on Nov 10 (CVSS 9.5). No public PoC or exploitation reported; not in CISA KEV. The prior RSC bug (React2Shell, CVE-2025-55182) went to mass exploitation. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Upgrade react-server-dom-webpack/parcel/turbopack to 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9 or 19.3.1 (and the framework release that pins them).

title: Git recursive-clone RCE via index path truncation (plus five more Git fixes)
why: Git and GitHub disclosed the fixes on Nov 10; no public exploit or exploitation reported; not in CISA KEV. No MSRC advisory seen for Git bundled in Microsoft developer tools. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Update Git everywhere (workstations, CI runners, bundled copies) to a fixed release and avoid recursive clones of untrusted repositories meanwhile.

title: AntiFox AI pentest platform (ARTEX fork) used to breach IIS web servers and steal AWS production secrets
why: Arctic Wolf Labs (Nov 11, covered by BleepingComputer and THN) tied AntiFox instances hosted on Alibaba Cloud to confirmed intrusions: IIS webshells, then a successful GetSecretValue on a production secret and S3 copy/delete. The IIS entry vulnerability is unknown and there's no CVE, so nothing for KEV. Microsoft has written about ARTEX, the parent framework, but not about AntiFox. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Hunt IIS hosts for new ASPX webshells. Rotate any AWS keys stored in web.config or logs. Alert on GetSecretValue and bursts of AccessDenied from new source infrastructure, and enforce IMDSv2.
product: Internet-facing IIS web applications and the AWS accounts behind them (abuse campaign, no product CVE)

title: Citrix NetScaler November fixes: Console unauth bypass (CVE-2026-120869, 9.4) and default-config ADC/Gateway memory overflow (CVE-2026-120868, 9.3)
why: Citrix bulletins (Nov 11-12) fix an unauthenticated Console auth bypass and a packet-processing overflow that affects every ADC/Gateway, default config included. watchTowr is building exposure checks. Citrix reports no exploitation, no confirmed public PoC exists, and none of these CVEs is in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Upgrade internet-facing NetScaler ADC/Gateway to 14.1-73.57 or 13.1-64.39 and NetScaler Console to 14.1-74.34. Until then, restrict Console access to management hosts.
product: NetScaler ADC/Gateway 14.1 before 14.1-73.57, 13.1 before 13.1-64.39; NetScaler Console before 14.1-74.34

title: Red Hat Quay unauthenticated signing-key takeover (CVE-2026-123710, 9.8) plus cross-tenant robot-token theft (CVE-2026-110697); no fixed release named
why: Red Hat disclosed the bug on Nov 11. An anonymous /v2/auth token can authorize service-key rotation, letting an attacker install a non-expiring signing key and forge tokens for every repository. Upstream fixes were merged Nov 11, but no fixed release was named as of reporting. There is no PoC or ITW report, and it is not in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Block /keys at the proxy so only trusted internal components can reach it. Review service_key_rotate audit events for keys with no expiration and remove any you don't recognize.
product: Red Hat Quay 3 and Quay 5 (standalone, Quay Operator on OpenShift, mirror registry for OpenShift); exposed when /keys is reachable by untrusted clients

title: Apache Shiro DefaultLdapRealm accepts any password when authentication caching is enabled (CVE-2026-129349)
why: Apache disclosed it on oss-security on Nov 13 (CVSS 4.0 9.1, network, no privileges). It is a Java library, not a Microsoft product, and it is not in CISA KEV. No public PoC or exploitation reported. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Find Java apps that bundle shiro-core with an LDAP realm and upgrade them to 3.0.2. Until then, turn off authentication caching on those realms.
product: Apache Shiro (shiro-core) before 3.0.1

title: Apache APISIX 3.20.0 fixes 7 flaws, incl. unauthenticated route-auth bypass (CVE-2026-124680) and identity-header spoofing (CVE-2026-124679)
why: Apache posted seven APISIX advisories on oss-security on Nov 13. Two let unauthenticated clients get past authentication in certain configurations. Not a Microsoft product, not in CISA KEV, and no public PoC or exploitation reported. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Upgrade APISIX gateways to 3.20.0. Until then, check for routes without auth that share an upstream with protected routes, and turn off forward-auth allow_degradation.
product: Apache APISIX 0.9 through 3.19.0 (124680); 3.18.0 through 3.19.0 (124679)

title: Firefox 160 / ESR 153.7 / ESR 115.45 fix 70+ memory-safety bugs incl. seven 9.6 sandbox escapes
why: NVD published the Firefox 160 batch on Nov 10 with seven CVSS 9.6 sandbox escapes and dozens of 8.8 use-after-free bugs; none is reported exploited and none is in KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Roll Firefox to 160 and ESR to 153.7 / 115.45 across managed desktops.
product: Firefox before 160, Firefox ESR before 153.7 and before 115.45

title: Node.js November 2026 security release: 16 CVEs incl. HTTPS cross-connection memory leak exposing TLS private keys (CVE-2026-123864)
why: Node.js shipped 16 fixes on Nov 11, seven rated High. CVE-2026-123864 lets an unauthenticated client read other connections' memory, including TLS private keys, and several HTTP/2 bugs let a client crash default servers. No exploitation or public PoC reported, and none are in KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Upgrade to Node.js 22.23.5/24.22.3/26.13.1, rebuild container images, and consider rotating TLS keys on HTTPS services that ran affected handlers.
product: Node.js 22.x before 22.23.5, 24.x before 24.22.3, 26.x before 26.13.1 (end-of-life lines always affected)

title: Zoom Workplace for Windows critical privilege escalation over the network (CVE-2026-108186, 9.6) and origin validation flaw (108187)
why: Zoom bulletins ZSB-26023/24 (Nov 10) rate 108186 Critical 9.6 with user interaction required. No exploitation or public PoC and not in CISA KEV. This is a Windows app but not a Microsoft product, so no MSRC advisory applies. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Push Zoom Workplace for Windows 7.1.8 or later to all endpoints, including per-user installs that bypass central deployment.
product: Zoom Workplace for Windows 7.1.0 before 7.1.8 (108186); before 7.1.5 (108187)

title: Copeland/Dixell XWEB EVO (EOL) batch: pre-auth root command injection and hardcoded backdoor password (CVE-2026-124002..124015)
why: VulnCheck published a batch of 14 XWEB EVO CVEs on Nov 12, including unauthenticated root command injection (CVSS 9.8) and a hardcoded admin backdoor password. This comes while the sibling XWEB PRO (CVE-2026-25085) is being exploited in refrigeration sabotage. There is no public exploit and no reported in-the-wild use, and none of the CVEs is in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 15: still not in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed: no new entries since Nov 14).
action: Take XWEB EVO web interfaces off the internet now, put them behind VPN or allowlists, and plan to replace these end-of-service units.
product: XWEB EVO refrigeration/HVAC supervisor, 4.3.0 through 5.8.8 depending on CVE; product line end of service March 2026
